findings.title: Authority safety fixture rejects a benign freshness bound
findings.detail: The authority test bans any dataclass field containing limit, so it rejects DriftPolicy.freshness_limit even though that field is only the explicit maximum evidence age used to reject stale research evidence. The executable import and call safety checks pass, and this lexical failure supplies no evidence of deployment, execution or risk-limit authority.

findings.title: Tamper fixture mutates the shared champion across tests
findings.detail: The tamper test changes rerolled.inputs.champion.role with object.__setattr__, but that champion aliases the module-level CHAMPION fixture and is not restored. A later regression fixture therefore receives ROLE_MISMATCH and becomes order-dependent; the LEARN implementation itself correctly rejects the contaminated input fail-closed.

findings.title: Proof-mismatch fixture also creates a self-comparison
findings.detail: Run 38 assigns CHALLENGER_PROPOSAL to the champion while the default challenger already uses that same proposal. The input therefore violates the earlier self-comparison invariant before proof binding, so SELF_COMPARISON is the correct deterministic first reason rather than the asserted PROOF_MODEL_MISMATCH. Give the mislabelled champion a distinct proposal identity whose supplied proof is bound to a different proposal, preserving both fail-closed checks and testing only the intended invariant.

findings.title: Transition-order fixture also supplies future evidence
findings.detail: Run 38 backdates effective_at to CREATED minus one day but retains the helper's default evidence, which is available only at EFFECTIVE. The evidence is therefore unknowable at the backdated instant, so EVIDENCE_NOT_KNOWABLE_AT_AS_OF is the correct deterministic first reason before the ModelTransition chronology guard can return TRANSITION_NOT_ORDERED. Supply evidence available no later than the backdated instant so the fixture isolates transition ordering; do not weaken either fail-closed check.

findings.title: Coordinated drift tampering bypasses revalidation
findings.detail: DriftResult revalidates only the current mutable input graph against equally mutable cached outputs. Changing accepted evidence severity from severe to mild and updating severity, adjusted_confidence, and abstain accordingly makes checksum() succeed; downstream comparison therefore accepts tampered evidence and restored confidence instead of failing closed.

findings.title: Evidence failure precedence depends on tuple order
findings.detail: _admit interleaves per-item consistency validation with duplicate-ID detection. The same evidence multiset containing duplicate IDs and an out-of-order timestamp returns DUPLICATE_EVIDENCE_ID in one permutation and EVIDENCE_TIMESTAMPS_OUT_OF_ORDER in another, producing different refusal checksums and violating permutation determinism.

findings.title: Internal commitment can be forged through the evaluator closure
findings.detail: The sealer is directly recoverable from evaluate_drift.__closure__. A caller can mutate evidence and all derived fields, invoke that sealer on the recomputed state, replace commitment, and make checksum() succeed; downstream comparison then trusts the tampered drift. The purported full-bypass test never checks this accessible path.

findings.title: Transition chains permit challenger-to-champion promotion
findings.detail: REINSTATE may omit reverses_transition_id and select any active next_role. A valid CHALLENGER→RETIRED transition followed by RETIRED→CHAMPION is accepted with final_role CHAMPION, violating the no-self-promotion criterion.

findings.title: Equivalent permutations do not produce identical results
findings.detail: DriftInputs and TransitionInputs retain caller tuple order even though checksums use canonical ordering. Equivalent evidence or transition permutations therefore produce unequal result objects with differently ordered inputs, contradicting the required identical canonical results; tests assert only checksum equality.

findings.title: Timezone-spelling fixture expects semantically unequal evidence
findings.detail: Run 43 converts every timestamp of plain into the America/New_York spelling of the same instant and leaves every other DriftEvidence field unchanged. Python aware-datetime equality compares the instants, so plain == spelled and the fixture fails before evaluate_drift is exercised. Assert that the timezone representations differ while the instants remain equal, then pin identical results; do not weaken timestamp canonicalization.

findings.title: Local proposal tampering invalidates the proof before model matching
findings.detail: Run 43 mutates the same proposal object used inside the champion's proof. The proof's own revalidation therefore fails first, so evaluate_comparison correctly returns PROOF_NOT_PROVEN before it can consider PROOF_MODEL_MISMATCH. Keep the proposal local and assert the deterministic earlier reason, then retain the later clean-fixture check; do not weaken proof revalidation or failure ordering.

findings.title: LEARN documentation omits a public API symbol
findings.detail: Run 43's LEARN documentation adds the feature narrative but omits the literal public symbol ModelRole, so the API-documentation contract fails at tests/test_brain_learn.py:759 before checking the remaining names. Add the missing public API name and verify every LEARN_PUBLIC_NAMES entry is documented; do not remove exports or relax the contract test.

findings.title: Invalid-policy fixture fails before the Result path
findings.detail: Run 44 constructs DriftPolicy with mild_confidence_factor=0.25 and severe_confidence_factor=0.75. DriftPolicy.__post_init__ immediately raises INVALID_POLICY before _drift can return the typed fail-closed Result the regression expects, so the intended evaluator refusal is never exercised. Align the fixture and contract so the deterministic Result path is tested, or explicitly assert construction rejection; do not relax the monotonic-confidence guard.

findings.title: Immutable-fixture guard rejects timezone.utc
findings.detail: Run 44 introduces an uppercase datetime.timezone.utc shared constant, but the immutability guard admits only str, int, float, tuple, datetime and timedelta, so it fails before behavioral checks despite timezone.utc being immutable. Inline or remove the uppercase timezone fixture, or narrowly admit exact timezone instances; do not allow mutable globals or weaken collection-order isolation.
